title: Squad Atlas (Payments) Onboarding
description: Week-one essentials for new engineers joining Squad Atlas, the team that owns Meridian's money-movement core.

questions.prompt: Which tool does Squad Atlas use to run its on-call rotation and page the primary engineer?
questions.explanation: Atlas runs its on-call rotation through Opsgenie; keep the app installed on your phone before your first shift (Squad Atlas — On-Call Runbook).

questions.prompt: What is the acknowledgement SLA for the Atlas primary on-call before an alert escalates?
questions.explanation: Alerts route to the primary with a 10-minute ack SLA; miss it and Opsgenie escalates to the secondary, then to the squad lead (Squad Atlas — On-Call Runbook).

questions.prompt: A scheduled payment settlement fails. What incident severity does Atlas assign it?
questions.explanation: Severity is set by impact to money movement, not alert volume. A failed settlement impacts money movement, so it is always Sev1 — never downgraded to Sev2 because 'only a few payments' failed (Squad Atlas — On-Call Runbook).

questions.prompt: Because Atlas handles cardholder data directly, which compliance regime does the squad operate under?
questions.explanation: Atlas operates under PCI-DSS Level 1 — the strictest tier — as Meridian's highest-volume card processor; every engineer completes PCI awareness training before production access (Squad Atlas — Compliance & Data Handling).

questions.prompt: How is card data classified in Atlas's data-handling policy?
questions.explanation: Card data is classified Tier 0 (Restricted), Meridian's highest data tier: it may never be logged, never appear in error messages, and never leave the boundary of services in PCI scope (Squad Atlas — Compliance & Data Handling).

questions.prompt: How does Atlas store the Primary Account Number (PAN) in its datastores?
choices: Encrypted at rest with a rotating key
Tokenized at rest — only the token is persisted
questions.explanation: The PAN is tokenized at rest: the tokenization service exchanges it for a token at the edge, and only the token flows through Rail into Atlas storage. A raw PAN found in a log, column, or trace is a Tier 0 incident — page on-call immediately (Squad Atlas — Compliance & Data Handling).

questions.prompt: When does Atlas's deploy pipeline refuse normal production releases?
choices: Only during the monthly audit window
questions.explanation: The pipeline is gated to refuse production releases Friday through Sunday — no Friday or weekend deploys. A fix that genuinely can't wait goes through the incident-change path with on-call lead plus Priya sign-off (Squad Atlas — Release & Change Policy).

questions.prompt: Which check must pass before any Atlas pull request can merge?
questions.explanation: The ledger-reconciliation contract test must be green before merge — it verifies that recorded entries match settled balances. A red result blocks merge with no exceptions and no override (Squad Atlas — Release & Change Policy).

questions.prompt: What is Atlas's primary datastore for the ledger?
questions.explanation: The primary datastore is Aurora PostgreSQL, chosen for strong consistency on balance reads and the durability money movement demands (Squad Atlas — Architecture & Datastores).

questions.prompt: How does atlas-ledger-svc apply a correction to a previously recorded ledger entry?
choices: Updates the existing row in place
Soft-deletes the row and re-inserts it
Appends a new entry that offsets the prior one
Edits the row and writes an audit log line
questions.explanation: The ledger is append-only: rows are never updated or deleted in place. Corrections are new entries that offset prior ones, so the full history is reconstructable from the table — which is what makes reconciliation and audit possible (Squad Atlas — Architecture & Datastores).

questions.prompt: What is the name of Atlas's primary service and repository, where the ledger and settlement workers live?
questions.explanation: atlas-ledger-svc is the primary service and repo housing the ledger, settlement workers, and reconciliation logic — new hires should clone it first (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership / Architecture & Datastores).

questions.prompt: What is the internal codename for Atlas's payment-initiation API?
questions.explanation: Rail is the internal name for the payment-initiation API exposed by atlas-ledger-svc. 'Submit it to Rail' means the entry point that accepts a payment instruction and hands it to the ledger (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership / Architecture & Datastores).

questions.prompt: Who is the squad lead and engineering manager for Squad Atlas?
questions.explanation: Priya Nair is the squad lead and EM, and the escalation point for ownership disputes, hiring, and cross-squad commitments touching the payment path. New hires should book a week-one 1:1 with her (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership).

questions.prompt: Where does Atlas store its secrets (database passwords, partner-rail keys, tokenization tokens)?
choices: AWS Secrets Manager, tagged by service
Vault, under the per-squad namespace atlas/
questions.explanation: All Atlas secrets live in Vault under the dedicated per-squad namespace atlas/. Nothing belonging to Atlas is stored outside that namespace, and secrets are read at runtime — never copied into code, a checked-in .env, a ticket, or chat (Squad Atlas — Secrets & Access).

questions.prompt: What customer-facing SLA does Atlas publish for payment-status availability?
questions.explanation: Atlas publishes a customer-facing SLA of 99.95% monthly for payment-status availability — customers must be able to see a payment's state (pending, settled, failed) within that target every calendar month, and a breach triggers a customer comms review (Squad Atlas — Charter & Ownership).
